# diffdevil App PR message — ratified design candidate and implementation handoff

## Meaning

This public source copy preserves the ratified PR-brief design and its accepted, proposed and deferred boundaries. Private Work coordinates are omitted; the executable specimens are unchanged. The local checksum manifest describes this public copy, rather than the original private transfer archive.

**Candidate:** `pr-brief-r4.1` · **Design authority:** Wolf and Nyxara · **Date:** 10 October 2026  

## 1. Standing and the decision that matters

**The enabled comment earns its place by showing useful information immediately. When eligible Pro context reveals a concrete connection around this PR, that connection leads.** The same comment still contains a useful current-change report. Measurement plumbing, complete evidence and general destination links live in one supporting disclosure.

Wolf ratified the Round 4 composition in this ChatGPT Web co-design: “Yep, this is good. I like this, and we should likely go with this as ratified for now. So please make this into a durable candidate and hand all of it off.” There is no shareable provider conversation URL. This quote is the owner’s ratification and Return authorization; the interpretation below is Nyxara’s design judgment.

The accepted object is the Round 4 content, reading order, native Markdown formatting and truthful state family, carried here as `pr-brief-r4.1`. The handoff combines that ratification with existing product contracts. **Numeric selection thresholds, control field names and implementation schedules below are clearly marked proposals; Wolf did not review or ratify an unseen algorithm.** Native GitHub rendering and the actual App writer still need qualification. This is a design candidate, not landed source or a live provider launch.

### Decision ledger

| Standing | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Ratified with Wolf | Useful facts before plumbing; prominent eligible Pro context; concrete related PRs/shared files/current contribution; selected file frequency and Turnover; an evidenced historical companion; useful current-change core; one supporting details fold. |
| Ratified with Wolf | One top-level native `NOTE` for the lead same-file PR connection, with meaningful headline inside its body; PR paragraphs; history table outside the alert; compact current-change block; no separate recurring Pro comment. |

### Why this is the accepted system

Round 1 made the reader pay a large chrome/disclosure/link cost for very little visible information. Wolf rejected that. Round 2 made the size report more useful, but still did not make the paid repository context feel valuable. Round 3 moved concrete repository connections into the lead and was accepted in content and reading order. Round 4 used native GitHub formatting to give those facts a clear visual hierarchy and was then ratified. The respectable pre-existing branding specimen remains background truth; it did not determine the composition by default.

## 2. Canonical message and compact/expanded composition

The default example is synthetic `example/relay` PR #452. All links beginning with `#pr-`, `#check` or `#app` are inert fixture destinations, not shipping routes. The source bundle includes the complete exact Markdown, pre-rendered design approximation, structured fixture and all variants.

```markdown
> [!NOTE]
> **Two open PRs touch the same files**
>
> **[#418 — Scope override precedence](#pr-418)** · open  
> Also changes `src/policy.ts` and `src/config.ts` — together, **68% of this PR’s included Changed**.
>
> **[#427 — Validate inherited limits](#pr-427)** · draft  
> Also changes `src/policy.ts`.

**The most frequently changed files in this PR**

| File | Changed here | Last 90 days |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| `src/policy.ts` | 100 | **18 merged PRs**<br>1.8× Turnover |
| `src/config.ts` | 68 | **12 merged PRs**<br>0.8× Turnover |

*Turnover is change volume relative to file size. The repository had **40 merged PRs** in this period.*

**`tests/policy.test.ts` is unchanged here.** It accompanied `src/policy.ts` in **14 of 18 merged PRs** touching that file over the same 90 days.

### This change

**248 Changed · Size M · 5 included files**

160 modified · 64 added-only · 24 deleted-only.

Other included files: `src/report.ts` (46), `tests/config.test.ts` (26), `docs/policy.md` (8).

`pnpm-lock.yaml` is excluded by repository policy.

<details>
<summary>Measurement and context details · c7a91e2</summary>

[Comparison, complete measurement and file rows, repository policy,
history window/coverage/support, Turnover basis, relationship meaning,
and descriptive links to the check and App. Complete copy is in the bundle.]
```

**Compact is the ratified closed-disclosure view.** The lead observation, selected context table, companion sentence and current-change core remain visible. The fold is for evidence and drill-down, not the place where the helpful message is hidden. There is no separate footer, repeated bot signature, upgrade panel or row of utility links.

**Expanded is the same message with its one native disclosure open.** Its order is comparison identity; measurement including raw churn; attributable repository policy; full included-file rows; compatible repository history and recovery coverage; frequency/Turnover/companion support; current-neighbour meaning; links to the native check and protected App detail. Expansion does not reveal a second report with different numbers. It is ordinary reader-controlled GitHub disclosure, not a per-reader App preference or persisted provider state.

The selected history table also reports those files’ current contributions, so the compact core says “Other included files.” Basic has no premium table and therefore shows its useful file contribution rows itself. This avoids charging the reader twice for identical visible data. Repeating full rows in expanded evidence is deliberate reference material.

No separate App density selector is required to reproduce this accepted product. If Account/Manage exposes a compactness setting, it must preserve this useful visible core. A larger visible budget is an implementation/design proposal, not permission to collapse all context or add dashboards.

## 3. Comment, native check and protected App detail

| Surface | Primary responsibility | What its existence does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One owned PR comment, when enabled | Help contributors and reviewers orient immediately: selected useful connections, current measurement/composition and named policy band, one evidence disclosure. | A review verdict, mergeability, predicted conflict, test sufficiency, or proof a desired GitHub effect happened. |
| Native check | Authoritative run/comparison measurement, repository policy evaluation, trust/freshness standing, and desired/attempted/observed effect status. | That a label or comment exists merely because policy requested it. |
| Protected App PR detail | Full comparison and evidence, lifecycle/run history, compatible history, all eligible neighbours/companions, selection explanations and analytical drill-down within viewer/repository authority. | Permission to leak private titles, paths, counts or existence into a public comment. |

The check and App link labels explain their destination: “Full measurement and effect status in the check” and “Explore this PR in the App.” Shipping links must bind the actual repository/PR/comparison and enforce the destination’s own access checks. Do not claim a check or App destination was created when it was not. A working comment remains useful if a protected link requires authentication. [S2, S3, S4]

## 4. Measurement and availability states

The bundle contains **12 complete primary specimens**: exact, bounded, partial and unknown, each with Pro context, basic history off, and basic history on. Extra acceptance specimens cover unavailable context, unavailable file population, stale head movement and an optional final summary. Unknown measurement and unavailable context are separate axes.

| State | Visible truth | Suppressed or qualified truth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact | 248 Changed; 160 modified + 64 added-only + 24 deleted-only; five included files; policy Size M; shared files contribute 168/248, rounded to 68%. | No quality/risk meaning. Raw churn 408 belongs in supporting measurement. |
| Bounded | 244–280 Changed; Size M because the entire range is inside the authored 100–499 band; report file 42–78; outward-rounded shared contribution 60–69%. | No exact replacement composition. A band is unresolved if a range crosses a boundary. |
| Partial measurement, complete paths | At least 202 Changed; four of five files measured; `src/report.ts` unavailable; measured shared contribution 168 Changed. | No whole-PR percentage, no fabricated total or size band. Missing measurement is not zero. |
| Unknown Changed, complete paths | Size unresolved; five known included files; independently valid same-file PR and historical facts may still appear. | No current Changed total, contribution share or exact composition. Complete paths still establish an unchanged companion. |
| Context unavailable or ineligible | Valid basic current-change report remains. An administrator can inspect why context is absent in preview/detail. | No empty Pro block, “no related PRs” claim, upgrade nag, or implied collection/entitlement enablement. |
| Current path population unavailable | State that the file list and measurement are unavailable. The check supplies acquisition/effect standing. | No five-file count, concentration percentage, whole-population superlative, absence claim or “companion is unchanged here.” |

Partial historical recovery is also independent. The copy must name the observed population and support, for example “among 27 recovered comparisons of 40 known merged PRs.” It must not claim a complete repository median or frequency population from those 27. Broad superlatives require a complete comparable candidate population; otherwise use scoped wording such as “Frequently changed files among the recovered comparisons.” [S2, S4]

The fixture’s `size@1` band is a repository policy result. **Unknown measurement does not itself mean that the size-label effect is held.** A policy can author `size/Unknown`; the check reports the actual selected decision and observed effects. The final candidate removes that unsupported inference from the earlier partial/unknown specimen. [S5]

## 5. Modules, eligibility and deterministic selection

The brief is deterministic, selective and bounded. It selects observed facts; it does not ask an LLM to review the change. Entitlement, consent, authority, measurement availability and actual support are independent eligibility inputs. A tier name does not guarantee a useful observation. [S2, S4, S6]

| Module | Product role and eligible basis | Behavior when ineligible |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current measurement and file contribution | Useful Free/basic core; exact/range/partial/unknown measurement and authored policy. Does not require persistent history. | Report the acquisition/measurement limit honestly; do not invent values. |
| Basic repository history | Compatible repository-level historical context, with separate history consent and available recovered population. The specimen uses median 132 across 40 merged PRs in 90 days. | Omit the comparison; preserve current facts. Ninety days is fixture context, not a ratified retention promise. |
| Same-file open PRs | Eligible funded scope and authorized current PR/file index. Show title, open/draft state, shared file identities and current contribution when defensible. | No fabricated relationships or false zero-results sentence. A semantic connection or dependency is not inferred from file sharing. |
| Selected file activity and Turnover | Distinct final merged-PR comparisons in a stated window; compatible scope; reliable file identity; per-file frequency. Turnover additionally needs period Changed and time-weighted average size. | Missing Turnover may become reasoned `n/a` without discarding independently valid frequency. Do not invent infinity or count unavailable size as zero. |
| Historical companion | Conditional co-change with an included anchor; pair count, anchor population, companion background frequency, comparable coverage, and complete current paths for “unchanged here.” | Suppress an absence claim when current paths are incomplete. Never infer a missing test or prescribe a file change. |

Pro/Business or an applicable funded grant gates enriched brief modules through the selected repository’s actual entitlement. A frozen preview is not live premium entitlement. Public Community keeps the useful basic implementation and common extension seams; premium implementations follow the parent Plan’s selected package boundary. No dormant premium body is to be published merely behind a false gate. [S6, S8]

### Selection contract and concrete candidate defaults

The accepted design establishes the module roles and useful visible relationship. It does **not** establish a universal “top two facts” rule: two neighbours and two files happen to be the accepted fixture. The following is **Nyxara’s bounded implementation proposal**, supplied so engineering has a concrete object to challenge and qualify rather than an empty “TBD.” Katja owns technical disposition; Nyxara owns any resulting product change.

1. Apply actual comment-audience eligibility before computing counts, ranking or copy. Apply repository inclusion policy and supported file identity before overlap/history calculations. Use one immutable current comparison and named context observation times.
2. Candidate neighbour support is at least one explicitly shared eligible file. Rank known current contribution ahead of unknown contribution, then descending share/contribution, then overlap specificity (shared eligible files divided by the union of both PRs’ eligible file sets), then a stable repository/PR identifier. Return at most **three neighbours** in the visible block. This is an ordering heuristic, not a conflict or relevance score presented to users. Broad-change and generated-file cases must be part of qualification; if this order selects noise, adjust the internal rule with evidence.
3. Candidate file-history support is at least **three distinct recovered merged PRs** touching that file in the selected compatible window. Rank frequency, then known current contribution, then stable path identity. Show at most **three file rows**. Claim “most frequently changed” only when the eligible touched-file population is complete and comparable.
4. Candidate companion support is at least **five anchor PRs**, at least **three co-changes**, conditional frequency at least **50%**, and conditional frequency at least **1.25×** the companion’s repository background frequency. Rank conditional excess over background, then support, then stable file identity. Show at most **one companion**. These deliberately conservative numeric gates are proposed, not statistically calibrated significance tests or ratified product settings.
5. Use at most five visible current-file rows/items where the context table has not already supplied them. Put a truthful remainder count and full eligible list in expanded evidence/App detail. These are per-module budgets, not a two-fact budget for the message. Preserve the useful current core if a module is dropped.
6. Candidate total body ceiling: **16 KiB of UTF-8**, including the disclosure. Trim lowest-priority optional observations/rows with an honest remainder before shortening the required core. Preserve valid UTF-8, Markdown, provenance and whole file identities; if a required untrusted value cannot be represented within the cap, use an explicit omission plus a valid destination rather than a misleading truncation. Confirm provider limits independently before shipping. When a visible neighbour cap omits matches, use “Three of N open PRs touch the same files” only if N is a complete eligible count; otherwise use the non-totalizing headline “Open PRs touching these files.”

The default fixture passes those gates: neighbour #418 shares 168 current Changed; policy/config frequencies are 18/12; the companion is 14/18 versus background 15/40. The rank, cap and support proposal must be replayed against broad PRs, tiny/sparse repositories, generated-file dominance, ties, missing measurement and partial recovery. It must not become an undocumented new policy language. A material change to which facts lead returns for Nyxara’s product judgment; exact adapter/cost details do not require Wolf to redispatch the work.

## 6. Lifecycle and owned-comment behavior

**Standard behavior is one App-owned upsert comment on an eligible open PR.** Comments remain off in ordinary managed setup. A fresh first eligible evaluation produces the useful full message immediately; history/context acquisition must not turn a valid basic message into an indefinitely empty placeholder. Subsequent eligible facts enrich that same owned comment. Existing modes and explicit triggers remain available to advanced repository-authored rules. [S2, S5]

| Event | Required result / candidate acceptance example |
| --- | --- |
| First eligible open-PR evaluation | Create one useful standard comment using available truthful facts, expected App author, target and rule lifecycle identity, and trusted effective policy. A stable host event/attempt identity supports reconciliation; explicit create/final-summary modes additionally need their stable occasion identity. If current acquisition is wholly unavailable, make that the actual message/check standing. |
| Own comparison or meaningful context change | Refresh the owned comment only after a fresh authorized evaluation. Relevant neighbour file/state changes, policy/brief changes and supported history changes can alter selected facts. Never append a second Pro report. |
| Same content or retry | Identical semantic render produces no write; the same create occasion cannot duplicate a comment. Attempt timestamps must not make identical facts appear changed. A meaningful historical window/evidence change can justify a new render. |
| New head while old result exists | Preserve explicit old comparison `b406d85` → `c7a91e2`. A pending check may say it awaits `f81b902`. Do not relabel the old numbers as the new head or mix newly fetched context into one supposedly current snapshot. The existing comment is left untouched until fresh reconciliation; its comparison identity stays available in its disclosure. |
| Stale completion arrives late | Freshness gate refuses its write. A delayed old-head completion cannot overwrite the current-head comment. |
| Reopen | Reacquire current state, trust and comparison; resume the same valid owned upsert lifecycle when identity is unchanged. Do not infer permission to adopt another author’s old comment. |
| Close without merge | Stop ongoing writes. Leave the last comment as historical conversation; no closing narration or repeated recalc edits are needed. |
| Merge | Stop ongoing writes. Persistent analytical storage may record the allowlisted final comparison under its separate consent; storage repair must not replay the comment. |
| Optional final merge summary | Explicit opt-in, proposed off by default. A separate terminal occasion emits one final factual summary from established merge/final-comparison evidence. It may be a separate terminal reply; it is not another ongoing report. No replay from imports/backfills; retries deduplicate. |
| Ownership malformed/duplicated | Stop reconciliation and expose actionable operational standing in the check/admin view. Copied markers or a similar-looking comment are not adoption proof. |
| Ambiguous provider create | Read back/reconcile the attempted occasion before another POST. Preserve desired, attempted and observed effects separately. A failed history-store write cannot duplicate a successful provider comment. |

The stale specimen in the bundle is a **read-only preview explanation around an unchanged old comment**, not a new stale-banner write the product must continually perform. The optional final-summary wording is proposed: “Merged · final comparison `b406d85` → `c7a91e2`”, followed by the final measurement/policy facts and one details fold. Use “merged” only from observed provider state; omit live neighbour/companion advice from terminal copy.

Advanced lifecycle vocabulary remains the existing one: `upsert`, `once`, `create`, `once-per-transition`, with mode and trigger distinct. `always`, `matched` and `band-changed` are not synonyms; a new head in the same band is not `band-changed`. An `upsert` matched condition becoming false leaves the prior comment rather than implicitly deleting it. Unknown conditions preserve transition state rather than fabricating a true transition. Imports and recalculation never replay historical comments, labels or final summaries. [S5]

## 7. Bounded standard controls, advanced wording, preview and migration

The standard brief is a designed product, not an empty template box. Administrators choose bounded behavior. The advanced route uses the existing portable language and trusted source mechanics. No second template language, arbitrary executable module conditions, or prompt-to-review control is introduced. [S2, S5, S7]

| Control seam | Candidate behavior | Standing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Comment mode | Off / standard brief / existing advanced portable custom route. Ordinary managed default is Off. | Off and two-layer distinction settled; exact field/UI vocabulary proposed. |
| Eligible context modules | Enable/disable supported module families within entitlement, authority, consent and data availability. Standard copy remains product-authored. | Bounded selection settled; exact control arrangement proposed. |
| Module priority | Small ordered set of supported priorities; deterministic, bounded interpretation. No authored expression language in the standard UI. | Implementation proposal. |
| History window | Choose from supported repository/service windows. Show effective window and consent/coverage. No implied infinite recovery or 90-day universal default. | Contract seam; available values need current service qualification. |
| Compactness | Ratified core plus one reader-controlled details fold. Any additional visible-density control must preserve immediately useful content. | Accepted reading states; additional setting deliberately not required. |
| Final merge summary | Separate explicit event, proposed Off default; terminal factual copy and stable dedup identity. | Optional event settled; default/control/copy proposal. |
| Effective source and writer | Show effective trusted policy/template source, semantic version, selected writer and ownership identity, plus migration standing. | Existing contract. |
| Advanced custom wording | Typed inline or trusted-file portable templates, policy/rule identity and existing modes/triggers. Standard editing does not silently overwrite repository-authored wording. | Existing route; no language changes. |

**Preview** uses the effective trusted configuration and expected writer, with truthful entitlement/consent/availability reasons. It exposes exact, bounded, partial, unknown, context-unavailable and file-population-unavailable cases; the same body can be inspected compact and expanded, and exact Markdown is available. Preview does not post, migrate ownership, enable history, grant premium entitlement, or assert fictional provider outcomes. Mark synthetic data explicitly in the preview shell, outside the specimen comment. Escape provider titles and paths as data, including Markdown/HTML delimiter and link-destination cases.

**Provenance** keeps comparison identity, context observation/window, recovered versus known population, effective policy/source/version, selected module support and actual writer/effect status inspectable. User-facing copy should include only provenance necessary to interpret the visible claim; complete trace and unavailable-module reasons belong in the disclosure/check/admin detail. Do not print new attempt timestamps solely to force a write.

**Writer migration** is a deliberate cutover: disable overlapping old writes; transfer the intended policy, templates and parameters; compare effective sources and managed names; establish the new trusted source and expected author; then observe a fresh evaluation and provider readback. Read-only Action/extension use can remain. Changing author/policy may establish a new lifecycle. Existing comments are not adopted merely because they contain a marker or look similar. Legacy cleanup is a separate explicitly authorized effect; enabling the App does not authorize it. [S5]

## 8. Data, history and privacy requirements

These are data needs, not new storage permission. Carry immutable comparison/base/head identity and measurement semantic version; repository inclusion/exclusion scope; complete versus incomplete current paths; per-file exact/ranged/unavailable evidence; raw additions/deletions; replacement-aware Changed; and reasoned uncertainty. Policy evaluation, desired effects, attempts and observed GitHub state remain separate fields. The adapter must never turn unknown into zero or desired into observed. [S3, S4, S5]

Neighbour context needs an authorized current open-PR index with stable identifiers, transient title/state, file identities, acquisition time and explicitly established overlap. History needs one unique final recoverable comparison per merged PR, merge-time window membership, known/recovered/omitted coverage, compatible measurement/policy scope, supported file identities and any rename limits. Co-change requires pair count, `subjectPullRequests` and `partnerPullRequests`; the conditional denominator is the subject/anchor file’s PR population, not the partner’s. The current analytical repair names those directions explicitly. [S2, S8]

Turnover requires period Changed and **time-weighted average file size** over the stated period, with identity/size evidence covering that period. It measures change volume relative to size, not distinct lines rewritten. A file created or deleted during the period has **`n/a` Turnover with that reason**, not a bounded numeric substitute. Binary or unsupported files and zero/missing denominators also need reasoned unavailability. Otherwise, bounded Changed/size evidence may support a defensible range; incomplete evidence must never imply fake precision. Frequency may remain valid when Turnover is unavailable. [S2]

**Audience filtering precedes aggregation and selection.** A public PR must not expose a private sibling’s title, path, count, existence or derived relationship, even if the destination link would require authentication. Viewer access to protected App detail does not expand the comment’s audience permission. Repository funding does not authorize another repository’s data. Recheck audience/entitlement during fresh evaluations; revocation and publication/redaction behavior need operational ownership and must not violate the closed-comment boundary by silently rewriting old conversation. [S4, S6]

Only the explicit allowlisted analytical projection belongs in persistent history. Do not retain rendered comment bodies, PR prose, custom templates or full reports/plans as analytical history. Transient provider text, protected configuration and operational ownership/attempt records have their distinct purposes and policies. Preview alone does not grant collection consent. [S4]

## 9. GitHub fit, accessibility and voice

Use GitHub’s native top-level `> [!NOTE]` syntax for the selected lead. GitHub supplies the fixed “Note” label; put the useful headline in the body. Keep the table, companion, size core and disclosure as siblings after the alert. Do not wrap the entire premium report or nest alerts. `WARNING`, `CAUTION` or other severity styling must not encode size, subscription tier, activity or contributor worth. GitHub’s alert semantics and restrictions are documented in its official formatting guidance. [S9]

Keep descriptive PR titles as links, full identifiable file paths as code, sentence-case headings, and ordinary semantic table headers. The accepted three-column history table places frequency before supporting Turnover, with a line break inside the historical cell and numeric alignment for current contribution. Meaning survives loss of colour/icon, and all facts remain readable in plain Markdown. Do not rely on hover, custom CSS, tiny text, badges or a chart renderer in a provider comment.

The reference offers desktop, 360 px and 320 px widths, but **those are preview choices, not observed native GitHub qualification**. The shipping candidate must be inspected on actual GitHub at normal/narrow widths, zoom, long paths/titles and with keyboard/screen-reader traversal. Verify table overflow, paragraph order, summary activation, link announcements, no clipped identities and Markdown copy/paste. Native provider CSS is outside our control; if the accepted table fails those checks, return a concrete stacked-row alternative for product judgment rather than silently shrinking text.

Voice stays concise, neutral and specific: “also changes,” “appears in,” “accompanied,” “included Changed,” and attributable “repository policy.” Never claim “connected” means dependency, shared files mean overlapping lines/conflict, a historical companion is a missing test, or a size band implies risk/quality/mergeability. No contributor shaming, automatic split instruction, mascot monologue or congratulations filler. Pro value comes from the observation itself; the contributor-facing block does not need a “Pro” marketing badge.

### Studio/client/engine evidence

This was a real multi-turn **ChatGPT Web co-design with Wolf**, using Nyxara’s pinned identity, complete composed boot doctrine, repository instructions, Studio source, the complete prepared Impeccable suite and current product contracts. It was **not** a target-launched Windows Studio engine encounter. Linux had no connection to `D:\code\diffdevil` or the maintained process-scoped Windows executable.
